title: Addressing the challenges of managing and monitoring biodiversity in High Conservation Value areas and High Carbon Stock forests within oil palm landscapes
content:
Protecting biodiversity in tropical production landscapes requires practical and effective management approaches. Through interviews and surveys with members of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO), this study explores challenges in managing and monitoring biodiversity in High Conservation Value (HCV) and High Carbon Stock (HCS) forest areas, and presents 15 recommendations to strengthen conservation practices. Field surveys, such as bird monitoring, play an important role in tracking biodiversity outcomes and informing adaptive management.


Abstract

Corporate commitments to biodiversity protection are difficult to achieve due to limited knowledge of effective conservation strategies and insufficient attention to the social challenges involved in fulfilling these commitments. We explore these concerns in tropical oil palm landscapes focusing specifically on the commitment of members of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) to meeting environmental sustainability standards relating to maintaining or enhancing High Conservation Values (HCVs) and High Carbon Stock (HCS) forests. Prior to developing new plantations, the RSPO requires that baseline assessments are conducted by licensed assessors to identify HCV and HCS forest areas for protection. Growers then develop management actions to mitigate threats to these HCV and HCS forest areas and preserve the conservation values and carbon stocks within them. We investigated the challenges that growers face in achieving these environmental sustainability commitments by carrying out online surveys and interviews of plantation managers (18 participants from 12 oil palm companies in Malaysia and Indonesia). We used findings from our survey and interview questions to make recommendations for improvements in managing and monitoring biodiversity within oil palm landscapes. Practical implication. Drawing on findings from our surveys and interviews, integrated with our knowledge of current policy and practice, we make 15 recommendations to help support biodiversity conservation, focused around four themes: (A) respecting human rights, including the rights to free, prior and informed consent (FPIC) and to participation in decision-making processes that affect people's rights; (B) standardising biodiversity metrics, with guidance on measuring biodiversity and analysing data on species trends, recognising that local biodiversity is highly dynamic; (C) building management and monitoring capacity and buy-in from oil palm companies through training and sharing of best practices; and (D) improving sustainability processes by incorporating information into monitoring and adaptive management systems, and creating open, transparent and standardised processes for regular reporting. We hope our recommendations will encourage the implementation of evidence-based practices that respect rights and incorporate local community perspectives, leading to better protection of biodiversity in oil palm landscapes in the long term.

Abstrak

Komitmen perusahaan untuk melindungi keanekaragaman hayati sulit dicapai karena keterbatasan pengetahuan tentang strategi konservasi yang efektif dan kurangnya perhatian terhadap tantangan sosial dalam memenuhi komitmen ini. Kami menelaah isu ini pada lanskap kelapa sawit tropis, dengan fokus pada komitmen anggota Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) untuk memenuhi standar keberlanjutan lingkungan terkait pemeliharaan atau peningkatan Nilai Konservasi Tinggi (NKT) dan hutan dengan Stok Karbon Tinggi (SKT). Sebelum mengembangkan perkebunan baru, RSPO mensyaratkan penilaian dasar oleh asesor berlisensi untuk mengidentifikasi area hutan NKT dan SKT yang harus dilindungi. Perusahaan perkebunan kemudian menyusun tindakan pengelolaan untuk memitigasi ancaman terhadap kawasan NKT dan SKT serta menjaga nilai konservasi dan stok karbon di dalamnya. Kami menginvestigasi tantangan yang dihadapi perusahaan perkebunan dalam memenuhi komitmen keberlanjutan lingkungan ini melalui survei daring dan wawancara dengan pengelola kebun (18 partisipan dari 12 perusahaan kelapa sawit di Malaysia dan Indonesia). Temuan dari survei dan wawancara kami gunakan untuk menyusun rekomendasi perbaikan pengelolaan dan pemantauan keanekaragaman hayati di lanskap kelapa sawit. Implikasi praktis. Berdasarkan temuan survei dan wawancara, dipadukan dengan pengetahuan kami tentang kebijakan dan praktik saat ini, kami menyusun 15 rekomendasi untuk mendukung konservasi keanekaragaman hayati, berfokus pada empat tema: (A) menghormati hak asasi manusia, termasuk hak atas persetujuan atas dasar informasi awal tanpa paksaan (FPIC) dan partisipasi dalam proses pengambilan keputusan yang memengaruhi hak-hak masyarakat; (B) standardisasi metrik keanekaragaman hayati, dengan panduan pengukuran dan analisis data tren spesies, sembari mengakui bahwa keanekaragaman hayati lokal sangat dinamis; (C) penguatan kapasitas pengelolaan dan pemantauan serta komitmen perusahaan kelapa sawit melalui pelatihan dan berbagi praktik terbaik; dan (D) peningkatan proses keberlanjutan dengan memasukkan informasi ke dalam sistem pemantauan dan manajemen adaptif, serta menciptakan proses pelaporan yang terbuka, transparan, dan terstandar secara berkala. Kami berharap rekomendasi ini mendorong penerapan praktik berbasis bukti yang menghormati hak serta mengintegrasikan perspektif komunitas lokal, sehingga meningkatkan perlindungan keanekaragaman hayati di lanskap kelapa sawit dalam jangka panjang.
